items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Johnny Williams playing trumpet at jam sessions in the George Lewis band, but the interviewee (Joe Darensbourg) does not mention knowing, meeting, or playing with Johnny Williams, only stating 'I always really went my way.'

ctx.x: to Buster's house, and even in the daytime, when we were in the Kid Ory band, until Buster died. And after that, I can't remember guys just having sessions. Everybody went their own way, you know.

No one has ever sort of brought that out about Ory's band. The George Lewis band, which was going around the same time, you often see tapes of them at parties with different musicians, and playing with young guys, different players -- Johnny Williams sometimes would come play trumpet at a jam session. But Ory... I've very seldom heard any tapes or recordings of anything. So you were corroborating that it was a band mostly, then, that sort of stayed to itself, and played professionally when it was working, and…

No. We didn't go out together anyway. I always really went my way. I remember one time, though... Once in a while, musicians, a famous musician would come up to Beverly Cavern, where we played, and the owner would let them sit in. I can't really pinpoint, except one of the highlights was Raphael Mendez. I don't know if you know who he is...
